transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in, and how have you been feeling lately?

I keep starting school projects and committee work with good intentions, but I can’t seem to follow through and finish things on time, no matter how hard I try to stay on top of it. It's started affecting my reputation at the school where I teach and is causing tension at home, so my wife and my department head urged me to come get this evaluated.
Have you struggled with these kinds of difficulties with focus and finishing tasks since you were a child, or is this a relatively new change for you?

These struggles actually date back to my childhood, though they've gotten much worse over the last 11 months with my new responsibilities. Even in primary school, my teachers noted I was always daydreaming and losing homework, and my parents had to sit with me just to get simple assignments finished. This pattern of attention and follow-through issues has persisted through university and my entire working life.
Along with these focus struggles over the past 11 months, have you also been feeling persistently down, sad, or lost interest in activities you normally enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I feel down or have lost interest in the things I enjoy. I'm definitely stressed and frustrated about my struggles at work and the tension at home, but it doesn't feel like depression.
Do you find yourself constantly worrying about many different areas of your life, like your family, health, or finances, and do you feel unable to control this worry?

No, I wouldn't say I have constant, uncontrollable worry about things like my health or finances. I definitely feel stressed and anxious, but it is very specifically tied to missing my work deadlines and the tension that is causing at home.
Alongside your struggles with focus, do you often feel physically restless, find it hard to sit still, or tend to act and speak impulsively?

No, I don't really experience physical restlessness or impulsivity at all. I have no trouble sitting still during meetings or while teaching my classes. My struggles are almost entirely related to my focus, attention, and keeping myself organized.
When you were a child, did you ever have trouble with being overly active, talking excessively, or acting without thinking, or were your difficulties always purely related to daydreaming and focus?

My childhood difficulties were purely related to daydreaming, focus, and organization rather than being overly active or talkative. My school report cards and my parents' memories just point to me constantly spacing out, losing my homework, and forgetting instructions.

opening_question.question: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in, and how have you been feeling lately?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a lifelong history of significant inattention, disorganization, and failure to complete tasks, with onset in early childhood (primary school) and persistence into adulthood. He explicitly denies any history of hyperactivity or impulsivity, both currently and during childhood. These symptoms have caused significant functional impairment in his occupational role as a teacher and in his marriage. Mood and anxiety disorders were ruled out as primary causes. This clinical presentation is diagnostic of Attention Deficit Disorder without hyperactivity, classified under F98.8 in ICD-10.
